decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to hold the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent while modestly slowing its asset purchases.

changes.quote: Fiscal policy is restraining economic growth, although the extent of restraint may be diminishing.
changes.explanation: The Committee noted that while government spending and tax policy are still holding back growth, that drag might be shrinking.

changes.quote: The Committee sees the risks to the outlook for the economy and the labor market as having become more nearly balanced.
changes.explanation: The Fed feels the economic outlook has become more stable, shifting away from earlier downside risks.

changes.quote: In light of the cumulative progress toward maximum employment and the improvement in the outlook for labor market conditions, the Committee decided to modestly reduce the pace of its asset purchases.
changes.explanation: Because the job market has improved over time, the Fed decided to scale back its monthly bond buying.

changes.quote: Beginning in January, the Committee will add to its holdings of agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $35 billion per month rather than $40 billion per month, and will add to its holdings of longer-term Treasury securities at a pace of $40 billion per month rather than $45 billion per month.
changes.explanation: The Fed set specific lower amounts for its monthly purchases of both mortgage-backed securities and Treasuries starting in January.

tone_quotes.quote: In light of the cumulative progress toward maximum employment and the improvement in the outlook for labor market conditions, the Committee decided to modestly reduce the pace of its asset purchases.

The Committee recognizes that inflation persistently below its 2 percent objective could pose risks to economic performance, and it is monitoring inflation developments carefully for evidence that inflation will move back toward its objective over the medium term.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 11.88% APR costs about $49.50 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.89% and moved +4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.46% would rise by about $7.12 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 6.9%, and employers added an average of 224k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.2% over the past year (November 2013); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.5%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -2 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.13% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that if the economy continues to improve, the Fed will likely reduce asset purchases in further measured steps at future meetings. For educational purposes, an educational forecast model gave the probability of a hold at 84%, a cut at 15%, and a hike at 1% for the next meeting.
